headline: Human rights activist Irene Khan appointed UN envoy with state minister rank
summary: The government has named the internationally renowned activist as Bangladesh's permanent representative to the UN, granting her the status and benefits of a state minister.
details: The government has appointed internationally renowned human rights activist Irene Khan as Bangladesh's permanent representative and ambassador to the United Nations.
In a notification issued by the Cabinet Division on Wednesday, she was granted the rank, salary, and benefits of a state minister for her tenure in this role.
Irene Khan succeeds Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury as the permanent representative to the UN.
She currently serves as the UN Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression.
Previously, she served as the Secretary General of Amnesty International, a UK-based international human rights organization.
caption:
From Amnesty International to the UN: Irene Khan takes over as Bangladesh's permanent representative with the rank of a state minister.

The government has appointed internationally renowned human rights activist Irene Khan as Bangladesh's permanent representative and ambassador to the United Nations.

In a notification issued by the Cabinet Division on Wednesday, she was granted the rank, salary, and benefits of a state minister for her tenure in this role.

Irene Khan succeeds Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury as the permanent representative to the UN.

She currently serves as the UN Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression.

Previously, she served as the Secretary General of Amnesty International, a UK-based international human rights organization.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline: 3 die, 251 hospitalized with dengue in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in dengue cases across Bangladesh in a single day.
details: According to a notice from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Wednesday, three people died of dengue in the last 24 hours.
A total of 251 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country during the same period.
The surge in cases highlights the ongoing challenge of managing the mosquito-borne illness during the peak season.
Health authorities continue to monitor the situation as hospitalizations rise nationwide.
caption:
3 deaths and 251 new hospitalizations in just 24 hours. Dengue is surging.

According to a notice from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Wednesday, three people died of dengue in the last 24 hours.

A total of 251 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country during the same period.

The surge in cases highlights the ongoing challenge of managing the mosquito-borne illness during the peak season.

Health authorities continue to monitor the situation as hospitalizations rise nationwide.
